high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 17 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rates across 34 Vietnamese banks as of July 17 shows rates holding steady, with no material changes from prior sessions — signaling a stabilizing rate environment. ACB leads the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits, also offering 7.2% for 9-month and 7.1% for 6-month tenors. Saigonbank ranks second at 7.2%/year (12-month), while Bac A Bank holds at 7.1% (12-month) and 7.05% for 6- and 9-month tenors. MBV, VCBNeo, and VIB all post 7.0%/year across multiple tenors including 6, 9, 12, and 18 months. In total, six banks are offering 7.0% or above for 12-month deposits. Just below this group, LPBank, BVBank, OCB, and PGBank each offer 6.9%/year for 12-month deposits, with LPBank notably offering 6.95% for 18 months.

high.title: SBV Governor Pham Duc An: The State Bank Has Had a Relatively "Tough" Time Managing Interest Rate Policy
high.summary:
At a high-level government conference on July 18 chaired by Prime Minister Le Minh Hung — themed "Removing Bottlenecks, Unlocking Resources, Boosting Growth" — SBV Governor Pham Duc An acknowledged that managing interest rate policy has been particularly challenging. Vietcombank Chairman Nguyen Thanh Tung raised five key concerns at the meeting: (1) insufficient capital allocation to meet credit supply demand; (2) structural funding imbalances; (3) rising cost of capital going forward; (4) foreign currency supply constraints and exchange rate pressures; and (5) issues surrounding collateral policy and local government borrowing affecting bank collateral assets. Tung also noted that achieving 10% GDP growth requires investment at 40% of GDP, while domestic savings remain below that threshold — implying a need for external capital. **Key implications:** The explicit acknowledgment of FX supply constraints and rising funding costs by a major state bank chairman signals continued upward pressure on VND lending rates and potential stress on the VND/USD rate. Bond investors should monitor whether the SBV pivots toward easing or tightening to balance growth targets against FX stability.

---

high.title: SBV Discusses Replacement of Banking Sector's Most Critical Circular — Basel Capital Standards Implementation Update
high.summary: On July 15 in Hanoi, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) convened its 6th Steering Committee meeting on Basel capital standard implementation, chaired by Standing Deputy Governor Đoàn Thái Sơn. The session included senior SBV supervisory units (Banking Inspection, Credit Institution Safety Bureau, Management & Supervision Bureau), legal and HR departments, representatives from major credit institutions, and the Big Four audit firms (KPMG, Deloitte, PwC, EY). The agenda focused on reviewing progress from the 5th meeting and charting the roadmap for replacing the banking sector's most important regulatory circular — widely understood to refer to Circular 41/2016 on capital adequacy ratios — with a Basel III-compliant framework. **Market implications:** A formal transition to Basel III will require Vietnamese banks to hold more and higher-quality capital, potentially compressing ROE and dividend capacity near-term. Banks with thin capital buffers may need to issue subordinated bonds or equity, increasing bond supply. This is a medium-to-long-term structural shift to monitor closely for its impact on bank credit growth, lending rates, and capital market issuance pipelines.

high.title: Approximately 80% of Vietnam's Banking System Funding Is Short-Term — SBV Governor Highlights Structural Maturity Mismatch
high.summary: At a high-level Government conference on July 18 themed "Removing Bottlenecks – Unlocking Resources – Driving Growth," SBV Governor Phạm Đức Ấn disclosed that approximately **80% of total banking system funding is short-term**, with medium- and long-term capital accounting for only ~20%. This creates a structural maturity mismatch, as corporate demand for medium- and long-term credit is described as "very large." The Governor emphasized that credit institutions must rigorously manage operational safety — balancing business access to capital against systemic stability — while confirming that the SBV has implemented proactive and flexible monetary policy to stabilize the currency, control inflation, and support economic growth. **Market implications:** This disclosure is highly significant for bond investors. The chronic short-term funding structure constrains banks' ability to extend long-duration loans without relying on the government bond market or long-term deposit mobilization. It also signals continued SBV caution around loosening short-to-long-term lending ratio caps (Circular 08). For VND traders, the Governor's reaffirmation of currency stability and inflation control suggests no imminent policy rate cuts are expected. Watch for any regulatory adjustments to the short-to-long-term lending ratio as a key catalyst.

high.title: Vietcombank Chairman: Banks Lack Sufficient Capital to Fund Numerous Large Projects Ahead
high.summary:
At a high-level government conference on July 18 chaired by the Prime Minister under the theme "Removing Bottlenecks – Unlocking Resources – Driving Growth," Vietcombank Chairman Nguyen Thanh Tung outlined five critical challenges facing the banking sector. Most notably for macro watchers:

1. **Credit supply constraints** – Banks do not have adequate capital to meet credit demand from large infrastructure and investment projects.
2. **Structural funding imbalances** – Asset-liability mismatches are creating internal pressure.
3. **Rising cost of capital** – Funding costs are expected to increase in the near term, a hawkish signal for lending rate trajectories.
4. **FX supply and exchange rate pressures** – The Chairman explicitly flagged concerns over foreign currency supply and VND/USD dynamics, signaling ongoing stress in the FX market.
5. **Collateral and local government borrowing issues** – Zoning and planning changes are impairing the collateral value underlying bank loans.

medium.title: Cash Dividend Record Dates for July 20–24: Highest Cash Dividend at 35%, Two Major State Banks to Pay Out Over VND 3,000 Billion
medium.summary: Approximately 30 companies will set dividend record dates during the week of July 20–24, with nearly 21 paying cash dividends ranging from 1% to 35%. Most notable are two major state-owned commercial banks: **VietinBank (CTG)** will pay a 4.5% cash dividend (VND 450/share) on July 24 record date, disbursing approximately **VND 3,495 billion** in total on August 27; **Vietcombank (VCB)** will also pay VND 450/share on the same record date, with total payout estimated at **VND 3,760 billion**, also on August 27. The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), holding 63.34% of Vietcombank's charter capital, will be the largest single recipient of that dividend flow. For equity and FX traders, these large dividend payments represent meaningful near-term **VND liquidity injections** into the banking system — a factor worth monitoring for short-term interbank rate dynamics and potential FX pressure if foreign shareholders repatriate proceeds.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Ring Gold Prices – July 18
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices rebounded on July 18 after a sharp decline in the prior session, though the pace of recovery varied across dealers. SJC gold bars rose VND 900,000/tael on both the buy and sell sides, reaching **VND 144.5–147.5 million/tael**. Ring gold (vàng nhẫn) at SJC similarly gained VND 900,000/tael to **VND 143–146.5 million/tael**. Other dealers including Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải and Phú Quý posted gains of VND 900,000–1.9 million/tael on the buy side. While gold pricing is a secondary indicator, elevated domestic gold prices relative to international benchmarks are a perennial concern for the SBV, as gold demand historically drives **unofficial USD demand** and can pressure the VND. Fund managers should note whether the SBV responds with additional gold import quotas or FX intervention if the premium widens further.

medium.title: Proposal to Retain Customer Payment Account Transaction Records for 10 Years
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) is proposing amendments to require banks to retain customer payment account transaction records — including transaction documents, payment orders, receipts, and account statements — for a minimum of 10 years from the year the account relationship ends. The move stems from Vietnam's commitments under Prime Ministerial Decision No. 948/QĐ-TTg and aligns with SBV's own action plan under Decision No. 1608/QĐ-NHNN. The broader objective is to comply with Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes recommendations, and to improve Vietnam's standing with the OECD and the European Union on international tax transparency standards. For international fund managers, this regulatory tightening signals Vietnam's continued effort to align with global AML/CFT and tax compliance frameworks, which could positively influence foreign investor confidence and capital flow assessments over the medium term.

medium.title: Bank Profit Update July 17: One Bank Posts 5x Year-on-Year Profit, VPBank Sets New Record
medium.summary: VPBank (ticker: VPB) reported record-breaking preliminary H1 2026 results, with consolidated pre-tax profit reaching nearly VND 18,900 billion, up 68% year-on-year and representing approximately 46% of its full-year target. Q2 2026 standalone pre-tax profit came in at nearly VND 11,000 billion — the highest quarterly core earnings in the bank's history. The parent bank contributed VND 15,600 billion in H1 profit (+45.5% YoY). Total operating income (TOI) surged 35.2% YoY to VND 43,400 billion on a consolidated basis. Total assets exceeded VND 1.5 quadrillion (VND 1,500 trillion), up 19.2% from end-2025, driven primarily by credit expansion — with the parent bank's loan book growing 24.6% to nearly VND 1.06 quadrillion. These results are relevant for equity investors in the VN-Index, as VPBank is a major index constituent; strong banking sector earnings may provide a positive re-rating catalyst for the broader financial sector and support VN-Index momentum.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 18 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank...
medium.summary: Private banks continue to lead the market on deposit rates, with ACB offering the highest at 7.3% p.a. for 12-month tenors, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. Six banks now offer rates at or above 7% p.a. for 12-month deposits, with LPBank, BVBank, OCB, and PGBank close behind at 6.9%. The "Big 4" state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) maintain a uniform 6.8% p.a. for 12- and 18-month tenors, trailing private peers by 20–50 basis points. Rising deposit rates across the private banking sector reflect intensifying competition for retail funding, which could transmit into higher lending rates and put mild upward pressure on short-end government bond yields. Traders should watch whether the Big 4 follow private banks upward, which would signal a broader tightening of monetary conditions.

medium.title: Vietnam Earns USD 4.8 Billion from Coffee Exports in First Half of 2026
medium.summary: Vietnam's coffee export revenue reached USD 4.8 billion in H1 2026, with June alone generating over USD 580 million from approximately 126,000 tonnes shipped. Export volumes grew more than 7% year-on-year, supported by rising demand from Northeast Asian markets including Japan, as well as Italy and Russia. While this is a strong trade performance, the market is cautiously monitoring potential supply-side risks in the 2026–2027 crop year due to El Niño-related heat and dry conditions flagged by the Vietnam Coffee and Cocoa Association (Vicofa).

medium.title: VN-Index Falls Below 1,800 — Liquidity Hits Bottom as Investors Await Catalysts
medium.summary: The VN-Index posted its third consecutive week of losses, falling 2.24% to close at 1,787 points, while the VN30 declined nearly 2% to 1,931. Market breadth was decisively negative, with selling pressure broad-based across banks, securities, real estate, steel, technology, telecoms, and industrial parks. A notable drag came from the Vingroup-linked stocks (VHM, VIC). Weekly trading volume fell sharply, with money flows into declining stocks outpacing rising stocks by a ratio of 2.13x. Foreign investors continued net selling. Analysts note that declining volume during a downturn suggests some exhaustion of selling pressure, and that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East were cited as the primary sentiment driver for cautious positioning.

medium.title: Experts Identify Oversold Stock Groups Expected to Rebound After Correction
medium.summary: Agriseco's Head of Research Nguyễn Anh Khoa noted that VN-Index's breach of the psychological 1,800-point support has pushed several fundamentally sound stocks into oversold territory, creating medium-to-long-term entry opportunities. The correction is attributed to geopolitical uncertainty, weak institutional buying in large-cap names, and continued foreign net selling. However, the analyst highlights that the low-volume nature of the decline signals fading selling pressure rather than panic distribution — a technically constructive signal for a potential near-term technical rebound. Relevant for equity positioning given the broader market weakness.

medium.title: Next Week is a Key Moment for Vietcombank, VietinBank, and BIDV Shareholders
medium.summary:
Vietnam's three largest listed state-owned banks — BIDV, VietinBank, and Vietcombank — are set to complete cash dividend record dates within a single week. BIDV locks its shareholder list on July 20 for a 4.5% cash dividend (VND 450/share), disbursing approximately VND 3,276 billion on August 20. VietinBank and Vietcombank both set their record dates on July 24, with VietinBank paying VND 3,495 billion and Vietcombank disbursing over VND 3,760 billion — both targeting August 27 as payment date. In aggregate, the three banks will distribute over VND 10.5 trillion (~USD 410–420 million) to shareholders within weeks. For equity investors, the ex-dividend dates will likely create short-term price adjustments in BID, CTG, and VCB — three of the heaviest VN-Index constituents. For macro/FX traders, this large cash outflow from the banks' capital base, combined with the already-flagged capital adequacy concerns raised by Vietcombank's chairman, reinforces the narrative of tightening domestic liquidity conditions. Monitor VN-Index performance around these ex-dividend dates and any knock-on effects on interbank VND rates.

---

medium.title: Q2 2026 Financial Results Update (Morning of July 20): Banking and Securities Sectors Post Strong Growth, Hydropower Sector Struggles
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking sector continues to demonstrate robust earnings momentum in Q2 2026. VPBank (VPB) reported pre-tax profit of VND 10,959 billion in Q2 2026, surging 76% year-on-year, bringing H1 2026 cumulative profit to VND 18,880 billion (+68% YoY). TPBank (TPB) posted a more moderate but steady Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 2,562 billion (+26% YoY), with H1 2026 totaling VND 4,668 billion (+13% YoY). Strong bank earnings are relevant for bond and equity investors as they signal improving credit quality, rising net interest margins, and a healthy appetite for government bond holdings on bank balance sheets. Robust bank profitability also reduces systemic risk concerns and supports a constructive outlook on the VN-Index's financial sector weighting. Investors should monitor whether strong earnings translate into increased loan growth, which could influence SBV's future liquidity management and interest rate stance.
